description: We are student innovators from Sekolah Tuanku Abdul Rahman (STAR) participating in the Junior Category. Ready to solve space challenges!"
summary:
What Did We Develop?
We created "The Sentinel of Hadley Base," a short animated video told from the first-person perspective (POV) of the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1). Through custom visuals, space ambient audio, and emotional voiceover, the video follows LRV-1 from its arrival at the Hadley-Appennine valley in July 1971 to its quiet, ongoing vigil on the Moon today.

How Does It Address the Challenge?
The "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge is answered by turning dense NASA space history into an emotional, accessible story for school-age audiences. LRV-1 recounts exploring lunar craters with astronauts David Scott and James Irwin and collecting the 'Genesis Rock.' It then explains why it was left behind—to conserve fuel and weight so the Lunar Module could safely return home—framing its abandonment as a noble sacrifice.

Why Is It Important?
Off-world hardware represents human ingenuity but often fades from memory. Our project ensures these silent pioneers are remembered. By transforming LRV-1 into an inspiring monument, it sparks curiosity in young learners, reminding the next generation that today’s missions stand on the tracks left by past heroes.
details:
How It Works "The Sentinel of Hadley Base" is a 1 to 1.5-minute animated educational video structured as a first-person narrative. Instead of relying on a third-person documentary narrator, the viewer experiences the history of Apollo 15 directly through the "voice" and perspective of the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1). The narrative unfolds across four emotional acts:

  1. Arrival (July 1971): LRV-1 awakens in the Hadley-Appennine valley as humanity's first wheeled vehicle on another world.
  2. Exploration: It recounts three days of traversing lunar craters and ridges with astronauts David Scott and James Irwin, culminating in the discovery of the ancient 'Genesis Rock.'
  3. The Farewell: It explains the aerospace engineering necessity of reducing spacecraft mass and fuel consumption, resulting in LRV-1 being parked permanently on the lunar surface as the Lunar Module ascends back to Earth.
  4. Legacy: Over 50 years later, LRV-1 remains a silent monument under the stars, inspiring future lunar explorers.

Benefits & Intended Impact Traditional space history can sometimes feel overly technical or inaccessible to school-age students. By combining verified NASA historical records with emotional storytelling, our project makes space science engaging, memorable, and easy to understand. Our intended impact is to spark curiosity in young learners—encouraging them to look beyond active space missions and appreciate the engineering sacrifices and human ingenuity behind the silent hardware still resting on the Moon today.

Tools, Software & Hardware Used To bring this project from concept to completion, our team combined historical research with digital multimedia tools:

  • Research & Data Verification: Official NASA Apollo 15 mission archives, lunar surface imagery, and historical technical specifications.
  • Illustration & Graphic Assets: Canva (for structuring visual layouts, custom lunar landscape vectors, and LRV-1 illustrations).
  • Video Editing & Animation: CapCut / google flow (for timeline animation, keyframe motion, visual transitions, text overlays, and audio synchronization).
  • Audio Production: Royalty-free space ambient music, cinematic sound effects, and clean voiceover recording captured via smartphone hardware.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered Our team’s core creative decision was personifying LRV-1—turning a mechanical rover into an empathetic storyteller with a distinct emotional arc (moving from excitement to quiet solitude, and finally to pride).

During production, our team carefully considered several key factors:

  • Historical Accuracy: Ensuring all dates, astronaut names, geological locations (Hadley-Appennine valley), and scientific milestones ('Genesis Rock') strictly aligned with NASA records.
  • Pacing & Tone: Balancing dramatic pauses, ambient space audio, and clear voiceover intonation so younger audiences can absorb the facts without feeling overwhelmed.
  • Privacy & Copyright Compliance: Ensuring zero personal faces or identifiable private details appeared in the final video, while exclusively utilizing royalty-free audio and original visual illustrations.
